payload.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=mechanisms+of+preference+formation+in+reinforcement+learning+from+human+feedback+RLHF+and+long-term+memory&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6928698\", \"title\": [\"Human Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback: Feedback Mechanisms, Meta-Collaborative Monitoring, and Identity Positioning in Long-Term Human-AI Collaboration\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This paper proposes the concept of \\\"Human Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback\\\" (Human-RLAIF) to describe how long-term interaction with generative AI may shape users' behavior and cognition within an evolving feedback environment. Drawing on the researcher's own collaboration records with a conversational AI system (a full-trajectory corpus of 1,611 conversation windows and 25,859 messages, of which 1,489 conversation windows and 24,304 messages constitute the primary coding corpus), this study adopts an exploratory longitudinal self-case-study design and identifies several possible patterns through thematic coding and aggregated trend analysis: (1) questioning strategies shift from direct answerseeking toward requests for structure, archiving, and longer-term rules; (2) the user side shows early signs of a reorganization of collaborative labor, while AI responses increasingly provide elaboration, organization, and scaffolding; (3) the user side exhibits more behaviors aimed at governing the collaboration itself, such as requesting risk reminders, reality checks, and explicit collaboration boundaries; and (4) identity-related change currently appears only as preliminary signs of shifts in identity positioning and role-based perspective-taking, which is insufficient to claim that stable identity transformation has occurred. The paper also discusses long-term risks associated with AI feedback, including confirmation dependence, pseudo-internalization, identity preemption, and the potential homogenization of expression and cognition. The claims advanced here are exploratory and mechanism-generating rather than statistically demonstrative or causally identificatory. To reduce privacy risks and case-specific narrative distortion, the main text relies on anonymized fragment types, coding labels, and necessary explanation rather than identifiable verbatim dialogue.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6928698\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6338238\", \"title\": [\"The Role of Foundational Autoraters in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF)&nbsp;\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>The advent of advanced artificial intelligence (AI) systems has fundamentally transformed diverse fields, including education, healthcare, and natural language processing. A particularly influential area within AI is Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), which leverages human guidance to optimize learning processes and improve model performance. In this context, foundational autoraters serve as critical tools that automate the evaluation of written submissions, providing essential feedback that guides the learning trajectory of AI models. This abstract explores the significance of foundational autoraters in the RLHF paradigm, focusing on their design, functionalities, and the implications they hold for enhancing AI systems.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6338238\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.7753/ijcatr1506.1001\", \"title\": [\"Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and Multimodal LLM Alignment: A Comprehensive Review\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.7753/ijcatr1506.1001\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 5, 20]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.36227/techrxiv.175382817.74693578/v1\", \"title\": [\"Fairness-Aware Offline Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (Fair-RLHF): Mitigating Bias in Human Preferences\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Offline Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback aims to train AI agents using predefined human data, however human feedback can be biased which can lead to unfair or sub-optimal decision-making. In this paper, we propose Fairness-Aware Offline RLHF (Fair-RLHF), a framework designed to integrate fairness constraints into Offline Reinforcement Learning. We aim to detect and mitigate bias in Human Feedback. This is done using causal graphs (DAGs), which help in analyzing and identifying where bias originates. This visual representation of the cause-effect relationship determines unfair dependencies and uses fairness techniques to remove them. Furthermore, fairness constraints are applied that use Pareto efficacy to balance fairness with performance, achieving the precision of 46. 5% and 84%. It is optimized by ensuring fairness and maximizing performance. This work provides a fair and efficient RLHF model that aims to bridge the gap between reinforcement learning, fairness constraints, and human feedback by developing a framework that ensures AI agents are unbiased and demographic disparities are reduced.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.36227/techrxiv.175382817.74693578/v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 7, 29]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "4b8e411b19136c2f1afc3b716c3d396e716ca870c76ab77740df40f73fd051c2", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "memory_formed_preferences", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.2139/ssrn.6928698", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6338238", "doi:10.7753/ijcatr1506.1001", "doi:10.36227/techrxiv.175382817.74693578/v1"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6928698", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6338238", "https://doi.org/10.7753/ijcatr1506.1001", "https://doi.org/10.36227/techrxiv.175382817.74693578/v1"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
